sources.title: Handling Update Conflicts — PowerSync docs source
sources.released_version_or_commit: Documentation repository main branch; no release tag or commit SHA displayed (UNKNOWN).
sources.locator: Handling Update Conflicts; ordered upload queue, PUT/PATCH/DELETE, idempotency, LWW default, backend validation, CRDT note.
sources.observed_operation: Opened source file and inspected the operation/policy sections.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Backend policy is unopinionated; a simple backend can be per-field last-write-wins. Upload operations can be replayed and must be idempotent. Backend may validate or ignore writes, such as updates after completion.
sources.applicability: Supports a PowerSync-style alternative only when custom domain reconciliation is implemented; directly informs stale-resolution and duplicate-write design.

sources.title: PowerSync Supabase Integration Guide
sources.released_version_or_commit: Documentation repository main branch; no release tag or commit SHA displayed (UNKNOWN).
sources.locator: Architecture and Configure Supabase; local SQLite/upload queue and row-level security passages.
sources.observed_operation: Opened current guide and inspected offline architecture/security passages.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Local SQLite reads/writes and queued uploads work offline in the guide’s integration; writes go to Postgres through Supabase Data API. It warns that without RLS, anon/authenticated keys can read/write all rows; explicit grants/RLS are required under newer project defaults.
sources.applicability: Evidence that offline persistence and access control are separate concerns; do not infer secure row scoping from sync alone.

sources.title: Apache CouchDB 3.5 replication and conflict model
sources.released_version_or_commit: CouchDB documentation 3.5 branch, stable URL; exact patch version not pinned.
sources.locator: Sections 2.3.2–2.3.7, default winner, _conflicts, deleted leaves, application-specific merging.
sources.observed_operation: Opened stable documentation and inspected conflict/model sections and REST API examples.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Concurrent replicated branches retain leaf revisions; ordinary GET returns only deterministically selected winner, while conflicts=true/open_revs exposes others. Resolution is application-specific and losers must be deleted explicitly.
sources.applicability: Key warning for CouchDB/PouchDB: replication transports branches but does not decide task/issue semantics.

sources.title: PouchDB replication and conflicts guides
sources.released_version_or_commit: Rolling guides; exact source commit/version UNKNOWN.
sources.locator: Bidirectional replication, retry, deletion and conflict resolution; append-only delta pattern.
sources.observed_operation: Opened replication guide and inspected result/guide text for conflict and append-only design.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Local/remote PouchDB can bidirectionally sync; winner is deterministic but conflicts remain; guide says app can surface or ignore them; document removal creates a tombstone.
sources.applicability: Relevant direct-replication alternative and reason to model meaningful change records so update conflicts are limited.

sources.title: Apache CouchDB database security API
sources.released_version_or_commit: CouchDB documentation 3.5 branch, stable URL; exact patch version not pinned.
sources.locator: GET /{db}/_security; members/admins and default behavior.
sources.observed_operation: Opened API documentation and inspected database-member defaults.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Members can read every document and write/edit non-design documents; empty membership permits regular document reads/writes. CouchDB 3.x newly created DBs default to admin-only.
sources.applicability: Warns that CouchDB member access is broad; roles and document-level validation/scoping require explicit design.

sources.title: PouchDB IndexedDB sequence/concurrency report and proposed fix
sources.released_version_or_commit: Issue #8599 opened 2023-02-10 against PouchDB 8.0/Chrome; PR #9093 opened 2025-06-16 with commit 2a54197; both Open when inspected, not a released fix.
sources.locator: Issue repro after more than 1000 replicated docs; PR report of parallel bulkDocs and metadata.seq; reviewer comment about absent named test file.
sources.observed_operation: Opened issue and PR; inspected environment/repro, claimed fix/test, and reviewer’s test-file objection.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Issue is a user report, not a universal defect. Proposed PR says parallel IndexedDB bulkDocs could leave metadata.seq below doc.seq; PR remained open and reviewer questioned the claimed test. No evidence reviewed that it shipped.
sources.applicability: Keep as a validation risk for PouchDB/browser adapter; do not describe it as fixed by v9 or as a verified general failure.

sources.title: PostgreSQL 18 INSERT and unique index docs
sources.released_version_or_commit: PostgreSQL 18 current documentation as returned by site; no Git commit applicable.
sources.locator: INSERT ON CONFLICT atomic behavior and partial-unique-index support; CREATE INDEX WHERE predicate.
sources.observed_operation: Opened SQL reference and inspected unique arbiter, ON CONFLICT, partial-index, and atomicity passages.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Unique indexes/constraints arbitrate concurrent inserts; ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE guarantees atomic insert-or-update outcome under high concurrency absent other errors. Partial unique indexes restrict uniqueness to a subset.
sources.applicability: Supports a proposed active-claim invariant in a relational backend; does not itself define fair/offline claimant adjudication.

sources.title: MDN PWA offline and background operation
sources.released_version_or_commit: Current MDN article; no release/commit pin (UNKNOWN).
sources.locator: Background sync event lifetime, worker termination, periodic background availability/scheduling.
sources.observed_operation: Opened PWA guide and inspected worker lifecycle and background-sync caveats.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Browsers may stop service workers; Background Sync may retry only a bounded amount/time; periodic sync timing is browser-controlled and may be absent. Offline content can be only as recent as last foreground/app refresh.
sources.applicability: A responsive PWA cannot promise instant/background delivery; show pending state and sync on foreground/open.

sources.title: MDN storage quotas and eviction criteria
sources.released_version_or_commit: Current MDN article; no release/commit pin (UNKNOWN).
sources.locator: Best-effort vs persistent storage and quota exhaustion.
sources.observed_operation: Opened article and inspected IndexedDB/Cache persistence and quota sections.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Browser origin data is best-effort by default and can be evicted; persist() request handling differs; quota overflow can raise QuotaExceededError.
sources.applicability: Browser drafts/photos need bounded storage, explicit errors, a persistence request where justified, and recovery path.

sources.title: CouchDB authentication and security guide
sources.released_version_or_commit: Apache CouchDB 3.5 stable documentation; exact patch version not in URL.
sources.locator: Authentication database, roles, cookie session, database authorization.
sources.observed_operation: Inspected primary documentation result while evaluating direct replication identity requirements.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: CouchDB’s _users database stores users; roles are user-defined and assigned by admins; per-database members/admins are broad DB permissions.
sources.applicability: Direct replication can be self-hosted but still requires a defined identity/provisioning and role strategy.

sources.observed_operation: Inspected an actual caller and its output on the closed issue page; no closure explanation was found in reviewed content.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: A single reported version/OS case; issue is closed, but closure is not proof of how it was resolved. Treat transaction grouping as a test question rather than a confirmed current bug.
